description: Supplement variants that the reference rejects with the expected outcome but before reaching the variant's target check, because of the reference's own evaluation or check order. Written by the supervisor; the variants and their expectations are unchanged. Each entry names the variant and the executor observation (the observation key used by the executor; '*' for every observation of that variant). The executor reports a listed ISOLATION? as ISOLATION-EXCEPTION and passes it; an ISOLATION? that is not listed fails, and a listed entry that no longer occurs fails as stale. Formulas left without a reaching vector are listed in REM-PARITY's TT-2 by the next text revision, as design D6 requires.

entries.first_check: Section 7.2's rule that every record and trailing filemark position the map describes fits in u64
entries.reason: The reference validates the covered prefix's positions, Σ(block_count + 1), before it forms T, and an Object whose T does not fit also describes positions that do not fit. Section 7.2 now states the position rule, so the map is invalid there first; T itself is never reached.

entries.first_check: the protected-range contiguity rule, evaluated in array order
entries.reason: The reference checks range contiguity in array order before the ascending rule. The text states the partition rule in ascending tape-file order and gives no check order (GAPS G-6).

entries.first_check: the Section 10.6 W = T rule, evaluated on the recomputed W and T
entries.reason: The variant keeps the recorded fields equal (5 = 5), so §10.6's rule as worded ('highest_protected_ordinal equals total_data_ordinals') holds and only the §7.4 cross-check should fail. The reference evaluates the W = T rule on the recomputed W (2) and T (5), and rejects there first; the second implementation reads it the same way (its BUILD-LOG, sup-32). Whether §10.6 names the recorded or the recomputed values is a text question for D9 (the GAPS G-1 class).

entries.first_check: the rescue precondition total = 2H + P + 1 with H > 0 (Section 13.3 step 3)
entries.target: the §13.3 tail location (total − 1 − H in the variant's construction; H + P in the current text)
entries.reason: Section 13.3 now locates the tail copy at H + P and requires the entry's total to equal 2H + P + 1 with H > 0; an entry that fails is not available. Here 7 ≠ 2·7 + 4 + 1, so the precondition fails first, no read is placed, and the construction's formula total − 1 − H is never evaluated. The rescue's specific failure is reported only as the epoch-level outcome, SidecarMetadataUnavailable{0}, which Section 13.3 step 4 makes the error whatever each copy's own failure was, so its detail cannot show which check fired. The tail rescue from the terminal index does not apply either, because a final ParityMap validates and its entry fails a precondition.

entries.first_check: the rescue precondition total = 2H + P + 1 with H > 0 (Section 13.3 step 3)
entries.target: the §13.3 tail location (total − 1 − H in the variant's construction; H + P in the current text)
entries.reason: As isolated-1, with H = 2^64 − 1: the precondition compares 7 exactly with 2(2^64 − 1) + 4 + 1, fails without overflow, and no read is placed; total − 1 − H is never evaluated. The epoch-level outcome, SidecarMetadataUnavailable{0}, cannot show which check fired.
